resources.string: Detects Reel elements inside Instagram and covers them locally. It does not use the Internet or store screenshots.

Short-form video can encourage automatic scrolling. Excessive or problematic use is associated with poorer sleep, reduced sustained attention, and more stress. This pause helps you choose intentionally.
StopReels can analyze the visible accessibility tree in Instagram.
Tap “Enable accessibility”, open StopReels, and turn on “Use StopReels”.

When Accessibility opens: 1) tap “Installed apps” or “Installed services”; 2) tap “StopReels”; 3) turn on “Use StopReels”; 4) tap “Allow”. Do not enable TalkBack or another app. StopReels only analyzes the visible Instagram interface; it does not use the Internet or capture the screen.
Take back control of your time
StopReels covers Instagram Reels to help you stop automatic scrolling. Media sent in private conversations remains visible.
It only analyzes the visible accessibility tree in Instagram: text, descriptions, view IDs, and element positions. It does not read keystrokes, passwords, or content from other apps.
No accounts, analytics, screenshots, or servers. Statistics are stored locally.
Enable Accessibility to start protecting your feed

Reels are not harmful for everyone or in every type of use. Current evidence associates excessive or problematic social media and short-video use with poorer sleep, more difficulty sustaining attention, and more stress. Many studies are observational and do not by themselves prove that Reels cause these effects. Taking breaks and limiting time can help you regain control.
U.S. Surgeon General advisory on social media and mental health
APA: health advisory on social media use in adolescence
EEG study on short-form video and attention (PubMed)
To make it work, enable the accessibility service. Then check the StopReels switches and the battery setting recommended by your phone.
Inside Accessibility: tap “Installed apps” or “Installed services” > “StopReels” > turn on “Use StopReels” > tap “Allow”.
In StopReels, keep “Block Reels” enabled. Leave “Block shortcuts” off so the notice only appears inside an actual Reel.
Tap “StopReels app settings” below > Battery > choose “No restrictions” or the least restricted option. Enable “Autostart” if your phone offers it.
✓ Accessibility is enabled. StopReels can now work over Instagram.
Covers real Reels in the feed and Reels tab, but not navigation or Reels shared by friends.
To disable Anti-Reels, wait %1$d seconds and then tap “I am sure”. Normal photos and posts are not blocked.

Android manages the accessibility service and it can keep working while you use Instagram even when StopReels is closed. On phones with battery management, choose the least restricted option, allow background activity, and avoid clearing StopReels from Recents.
Tap “StopReels app settings” and open Battery. Choose “No restrictions” if available. No additional permanent process is started.
Open “StopReels app settings”. Under Battery choose “No restrictions” or the least restricted option and enable “Autostart” if available. Names vary by manufacturer and Android version.
English is the default. Choose another language for the app interface.
Optional. Can cover buttons that open Reels; leave it off so the notice only appears inside an actual Reel.
Blocks Reels detected while browsing Home.
Blocks the Reels viewer, but not the button used to enter it.
Shows a Reel for a limited time after confirmation.
After tapping to view a Reel, wait this long before you can confirm the temporary unlock.
Optional. Stories are not blocked by default.
Optional. Blocks videos that are not identified as Reels.
Keeps photos and videos shared in Direct conversations visible.
Shows the detected element type on the blocking notice.
Enables blocking only inside the selected time interval.
Limits temporary-unlock minutes per day. Choose “Off” for no limit.
Both counters will be reset to zero.

The service only observes com.instagram.android on the active screen. It uses interface signals — text, accessibility, IDs, and structure — to estimate whether an element is a Reel. When there is a sufficient signal, it places a local opaque cover.
StopReels looks for conversation signals such as Direct, chat, conversation, and the message field. If the context looks like a chat, it does not cover shared media even if its text mentions a Reel.

Instagram can change its hierarchy, labels, or IDs without notice. Blocking cannot be perfect: a Reel may be missed or an unexpected shortcut may be covered. Detection stays conservative to protect private messages and normal posts.
Turn off “Block Reels” inside StopReels or disable StopReels from Android Settings > Accessibility > Installed apps.
StopReels has no account, server, ads, purchases, or analytics. It does not scrape Instagram or store its content. It only stores your preferences and counters locally.
